correctness.rationale: Any two distinct points are on a unique line and any two lines meet at one point. Thus a pair of adjacent edges is the unique two-step geodesic between its other endpoints; strong rainbow colouring forces propriety, including with the fourth colour. A nonincident point–line pair has precisely three geodesics of length three, one per point on the target line. Consequently only the 28 nonincidences need testing once propriety holds. I independently enumerated colour permutations at each point, discarding line conflicts and normalizing at point 0. There are eight classes, the eight frozen obstruction strings all match, each failed set is a bijection of points to nonincident lines, and every nonincidence occurs twice. A second recursion generated matchings as partial injections of points into incident lines. For each geodesic and input colouring I tested admissible intersections with the matching: zero recoloured edges if the original path is rainbow, one if the two retained colours differ, never two or more. This reproduced the all-matching vector (1,21,168,644,1218,1050,336,24) and the success vector (0,0,0,0,126,84,0,0) for each of the eight classes. The specific frozen four-colour witness passed. Palette renaming multiplies the class count by 6 and preserves successes. Nonmatching recolourings cannot avoid adjacent new-colour conflicts, so the four-edge minimum is exact within the specified model and src(H)=4.
residual_risks: The full census is for one fresh colour and one fixed proper 3-colouring at a time, not for general recolouring or arbitrary four-colourings.

value.rationale: The canonical cubic Fano incidence graph is a natural distance-three test case. Beyond the optimal value, the obstruction incidence pattern and full repair polynomial measure how a standard proper colouring can be changed to make all distances work. The loss of all successes again at six or seven recolourings is a meaningful nonmonotone effect, not implied by the existence of one successful repair.
residual_risks: Finite invariant of this graph in a precisely restricted repair model; no extension to other cages or general repair schemes is asserted.
